title: BEA's early AI estimates separate measurement limits, realized use, output, and industry cost shifts
source_unit: BEA-BLS-Census-Gallup industry accounts, state-industry cells, and industry-year production-account observations
geography: United States; industries and state-by-industry cells

observations.period: 2026; BEA early estimates within industry economic accounts

baseline_pattern.value: productivity enhancing and input saving; associated with shift toward younger, relatively less educated workers

alternative_timing.value: less robust and also suggests labor saving

direct_ai_line_item.value: not currently available in US national accounts

observations.method: Indirect estimation through BEA industry accounts using Census-based AI measures; baseline and alternative timing/pervasiveness specifications are compared.
observations.uncertainty: BEA labels the results early estimates and emphasizes measurement challenges; timing assumptions, indirect measurement, input substitution, worker composition, and unmeasured AI costs limit causal interpretation.
observations.subgroup: US industries and worker-composition categories, including younger/older and relatively less/more educated workers.
observations.counterinterpretation: The alternative specification is less robust and industry-account associations may reflect timing, composition, or other input changes rather than AI itself.

observations.period: 2016-2024 outcomes linked to Q2 2025-Q1 2026 AI utilization; BEA WP2026-18

denominator.unit: Gallup Workforce Panel worker observations used to construct state-industry utilization; 52,729 in Q2-Q4 2025 and 22,563 in Q1 2026

employment_semielasticity.unit: percent employment difference per 1 percentage-point higher frequent-user share

real_output_semielasticity.unit: percent real-output difference per 1 percentage-point higher frequent-user share

observations.method: State-by-industry worker-reported frequent AI use from Gallup linked to LEHD employment/earnings and BEA real output; state×industry and industry×year fixed effects; industry-only BTOS specification is compared.
observations.uncertainty: The paper states estimates are descriptive rather than causal. AI utilization is measured after much of the outcome window, employment is noisy, state-industry cells vary in precision, and the industry-only BTOS specification does not reproduce the output pattern.
observations.subgroup: US states, two-digit industries, worker-reported frequent AI users, and employer-reported industry AI use; outcomes include employment, earnings, and real output.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reverse causality, managerial quality, complementary intangible capital, local demand, measurement differences, and cell composition can produce positive associations without an AI effect.

observations.period: 1997-2023 industry accounts; 2022-2023 post period; BEA WP2026-8
observations.method: Imputation-based difference-in-differences using BEA-BLS integrated industry-level production accounts; AI-intensity quartiles based on Census measures at 19-sector level, with industry/year effects and standard errors clustered by sector.
observations.uncertainty: BEA presents early exploratory evidence, not a causal estimate. Industry intensity, imputation, equal weighting, clustered inference, price/cost decomposition, and unmeasured AI costs limit interpretation; an alternative 2018 intensity definition is not identical.
observations.subgroup: AI-intensive versus other private industries; college/noncollege labor, capital, materials, energy, and services input categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower output-price growth may reflect pre-existing industry differences, input prices, demand, composition, or unmeasured costs and does not establish that households received lower prices.

related_sources.claim: BEA identifies AI utilization, production accounts, capital/data assets, prices, productivity, and digital trade as developing measurement domains.
BEA provides the formal citation for WP2026-18 AI Utilization and Economic Performance.
Registered BEA methods and definitions landing page for national-account interpretation.

boundary: This record separates three BEA evidence roles: indirect early industry-account estimates, descriptive state-industry utilization associations, and imputation-based industry cost/price estimates. It does not establish a general causal AI productivity effect, household price pass-through, worker control, employment change, or political consequence. The records must not be pooled across units or interpreted as one BEA estimate.
